Brunel University of London was established in 1966 and is a leading multidisciplinary research-intensive technology university delivering economic, social and cultural benefits.

The new appointment will be associated with the internationally recognised Brunel Interdisciplinary Power Systems (BIPS) Research Centre within the Department of Engineering. The College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences (CEDPS) is one of the largest and most successful in the UK, with close to 5,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students. Department of Engineering is a vibrant and successful Department within CEDPS.

We are looking to recruit a Research Assistant / Research Fellow to work on projects (1) “Climate Resilient Heat Electrification for Net-Zero Emission Whole Energy Systems (RENEW)”, funded by UKRI; and (2) “Benefits and Lifecycle-analysis of Underground Energy Storage Technologies for net zero (BLUEST)”, funded by the UK Energy Research Centre (UKERC). Applicants are expected to hold a PhD in an appropriate area and have expertise in one or more of the following areas: energy system modelling and optimisation, power system analysis, renewable energy, transmission and distribution system operation, energy storage, low-carbon energy technologies or other closely related areas. You will be a self-motivated, but highly collaborative researcher. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, fluency in English and an ability to work independently are essential. Candidates will be expected to demonstrate a good track record in project management, presenting their work, report writing and research publications. Outstanding candidates without a PhD, but having directly relevant research or practical experience are also welcome to apply.

Newcastle, GB

Research Assistant: £34,630 to £36,320 per annum

Research Associate: £37,369 to £41,885 per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 12 November 2026

 

 

The Role

 

We are seeking an enthusiastic Research Assistant/Associate to join an exciting Innovate UK-funded feasibility project focused on developing sustainable electrode materials for vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs).

 

The collaboration between Newcastle University and industry partners explores the potential of utilising waste-derived carbon materials into investigate the application of waste-derived carbon materials in high-performance electrodes for energy storage applications.

 

You will play a key role in accelerating the development and commercialisation of low-cost VRFB electrodes, supporting the growth of the UK's vanadium flow cell battery electrode supply chain and enhancing our global competitiveness in the energy storage market. This project will be conducted within the School of Engineering at Newcastle University.

 

This post is full-time and fixed term for up to 12 months (but no later than 31/10/2027). You are expected to take up the post from as soon as possible. 

 

To apply please submit your up-to-date CV and a cover letter (maximum of two A4 pages). The cover letter should include a description of how you meet the key criteria. Interview will be organised soon after the closing date.

 

Some travel may be required to attend conferences and meetings with collaborators. Pre-employment checks will be conducted before any job offer is made.

 

For informal discussions and queries, prospective applicants can contact Professor Anh Phan (the lead investigator of the project) at anh.phan@newcastle.ac.uk.

 

As part of our commitment to career development for research staff, the University has developed 3 levels of research role profiles.  These profiles set out firstly the generic competences and responsibilities expected of role holders at each level and secondly the general qualifications and experiences needed for entry at a particular level.

 

Newcastle University is committed to the responsible use of research metrics as part of our research culture and research strategy. We advocate for the transparent, appropriate, and inclusive use of metrics, guided by expert judgment, to support high-quality, impactful research that is open, collaborative and sustainable. Click here for our full policy statement on the Responsible use of Research Metrics. Click here for a self-study e-learning module on the Responsible Use of Research Metrics.

Research Assistant

Characterise waste-derived carbon materials using various techniques such as SEM, Raman spectroscopy, XRD, BET surface area analysis, elemental analysis, and other relevant methods
Formulate and fabricate electrode materials for flow battery applications
Conduct electrochemical testing and analysis
Design, assemble, commission a laboratory-scale vanadium redox flow battery test rig and evaluate prototype performance, efficiency, and durability
Work closely with industrial partners on project milestones and deliverables
Collect, analyse and interpret research data and draw conclusions on the outcomes
Co-ordinate own work with that of others, use problem solving to affect the achievement of research objectives and contribute to the planning of the project(s)
Present information on research progress and outcomes to a Principal Investigator and/or groups overseeing the research project
Write up results from own research activity and provide input into the research project’s dissemination (report, papers, chapters, books)
Use research resources (including, where required, laboratories, workshops and specialist equipment) as appropriate

 

 

In addition for Research Associate

Contribute ideas, including enhancements to the technical or methodological aspects of the project
Determine appropriate methodologies for research
Assess research findings for the need/scope for further investigations
Contribute to the writing up of the research and its dissemination, either through seminar and conference presentations and through publications
Present research findings, at conferences, publications in reputable outlets appropriate to the discipline
Contribute to grant applications submitted by Principle Investigator, others (if applicable) and develop own research objectives and proposals for funding

 Knowledge, Skills and Experience

 

 

Research Assistant

   Experience in electrochemical testing and analysis
   Experience in advanced functional materials, carbon materials characterisation and electrode engineering
   Experience in redox flow batteries (ideally vanadium), other battery technologies, fuel cells or electrolysers
   Experience of working with industry

   Ability to present complex information effectively to a range of audiences

   Experience of working collaboratively with colleagues

   The ability to use personal initiative and creativity to solve research problems

Advanced knowledge of electrode engineering, flow battery technologies, materials characterisation and electrochemistry
Experience in prototype development and engineering scale-up
Ability to write peer reviewed journals and drive research agenda independentl
Experience of working in a laboratory environment
Awareness of the research environment
High level of analytical and problem-solving capacity
Ability to communicate complex information with clarity
Experience of presentations at conferences and/or in high quality publications

 

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Commitment to working positively as a member of a multi-skilled research team
Ability to negotiate and prioritise multiple, competing responsibilities and to work to deadlines
Commitment to continued professional development
Understanding of good practice in equality, inclusion and diversity
The ability to take the initiative in pursuit of agreed objectives
Willingness to work flexibly (when appropriate) by mutual agreement

Willingness to supervise Master and PhD students

PhD near to completion in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrochemistry or a closely related discipline

The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to join the Infectious Disease Epidemiology & Dynamics department at LSHTM to work on Polio Eradication. The post-holder will develop and parameterize models of poliovirus transmission, with the aim of capturing the spatial patterns of observed cases and improving understanding of drivers of transmission. Data are available from collaborators to parameterize models, including disease surveillance and demography data from affected countries. The models will be used to inform and evaluate vaccination strategies that expedite polio eradication. The post-holder will work closely with partners within the Global Polio Eradication Initiative. This role is funded by the Gates Foundation.  

Responsibilities will include conducting epidemiological analyses relevant to polio eradication, predominantly in low-income countries, and managing the development and collection of data relevant to the transmission of childhood infectious diseases in low-income countries. Applicants will have a postgraduate degree, ideally a doctoral degree in a relevant topic, and demonstrable experience in constructing compartmental models of infectious diseases and fitting to data.

The post is full-time 35 hours per week, 1.0 FTE and fixed term until 30 September 2027 with the possibility of an extension subject to funding. The post is funded by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and is available from 01 November 2026.

The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, Grade 6 in the range £46,643 - £52,909 per annum pro rata (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London at LSHTM.

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference EPH-EPED-2026-09. 

The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. 

Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date.

Aston Business School

This position offers a unique opportunity for a highly motivated individual to work at the interface of academia and industry in a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate role that will deliver transformational impact. You will lead and deliver a service innovation programme within a fast-growing British SME manufacturer, helping to drive innovation and business growth in a company with strong values centred on teamwork, innovation, and excellence.

The project is fundamentally focused on servitization; supporting an engineering company transition from providing equipment through traditional capital expenditure (CapEx) systems towards a service-led, lifecycle-oriented business model. You will lead the co-design and implementation of a product-service system within the company, developing service-led concepts and offerings that create value for customers over the lifecycle of their operations.

This role is designed to enable the transition of a company towards a service-led business model, developing new forms of value creation and strengthening long-term customer relationships. You will play a key role in establishing the foundations for ongoing servitization, embedding new capabilities, and supporting the sustainable growth of the business beyond the duration of the KTP.

Candidate Profile: 

A minimum of a 2:1 BSc degree in Engineering or Management, or a related discipline.  

 Essential skills, experience and attributes required include:

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to work across technical and commercial domains
Experience of adapting theories and/or tools to commercial practice
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to engage across multiple levels of an organisation
Strong project management capability, able to manage complex projects, coordinate roles, and work independently, as well as part of the team.

Knowledge or experience of servitization, product-service systems, or business model innovation.
Experience of working in manufacturing or industrial settings.
Experience in customer research, data analysis, or development of commercially informed strategies.

Key responsibilities of this role include: 

Service design and product-service system development
Servitization strategy development
Commercial and go-to-market activities
Customer and stakeholder engagement
Knowledge transfer and embedding
Academic contribution to conference papers/ journal publications

See the job description for full details of the responsibilities associated with this role.

Up to £4,000 for personal and professional development for the duration of the project
Annual leave (25 days p/a)
Professional support and mentorship
Mental Health and wellbeing support: https://www.aston.ac.uk/staff-public/hr/Benefits-and-Rewards/health-wellbeing 
A flexible blend of on-site and remote working arrangements can be negotiated in case of positive ongoing performance.

This role opens up exciting career opportunities in new business development and servitization. Over 60% of our KTP associates are offered employment by their host companies at the end of the KTP. 

This is a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP). It is essential you understand how KTP works and the vital role you will play if you secure this position. To learn more please visit: www.aston.ac.uk/ktp

The Company: A Birmingham-based, industry-leading manufacturer, specialised in engineering and producing material handling equipment.

Aston University: You will work in a project team consisting of Dr Reza Marvi, Dr Geoff Parkes, Dr Daniel Andrews from Aston University and the Senior Management Team of the Company, with the support of a Knowledge Transfer Adviser from Innovate UK.

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 12 November 2026

 

 

The Role

 

The Environmental Biotechnology Innovation Centre (EBIC - https://ebicentre.co.uk/ ), of which ICOS ( https://ico2s.org ) is a member, brings together scientists from leading UK institutions in a mission to engineer the properties and functions of microorganisms, creating more effective ways to monitor the environment, remove pollutants and support a circular bioeconomy.

 

We are seeking a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to manage the experimental delivery of an AI- and bioinformatics-augmented, high-throughput platform for discovering and engineering enzymes that depolymerise polyethylene terephthalate (PET). PETase-like sequences will be prioritised, expressed, screened and improved through rapid Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) cycles.

 

You will combine synthetic biology, enzyme engineering, and bioinformatics to improve PETase, MHETase/BHETase, and PET-binding modules for PET degradation.

 

You will work closely with Professor Natalio Krasnogor, the wider ICOS and EBIC teams and international collaborators at PROIMI-CONICET in Argentina. You will establish reproducible protocols and structured data capture, coordinate delivery against milestones, publish high-quality research and help translate the platform towards industrially credible PET valorisation. Appointment at Senior Research Associate level will reflect a stronger record of independent management, supervision, partnership working, translation, research development and commercial/industrial experience.

 

This post includes travel within the UK and internationally, including visits to collaborator laboratories and conferences, as required for the project and subject to reasonable adjustments.

 

A completed doctorate in a relevant discipline is essential for appointment at either level.

 

For an informal conversation about the opportunity, please contact Professor Natalio Krasnogor at Natalio.Krasnogor@newcastle.ac.uk.

 

This role is full time, fixed term for a period up to 31.03.29

 

To apply, please upload a CV and letter of application which outlines how your skills, experiences and knowledge align with the person specification below.

 

 

 

Key Accountabilities 

 

For Research Associate and Senior Research Associate:

 

Steer the development of an end-to-end, experimental reproducible workflow for PETase discovery and optimisation, from candidate sequence to experimentally validated enzyme performance
Apply bioinformatic filtering, active-site and motif analysis, structure prediction, clustering and diversity-aware selection to prioritise compost-metagenome-derived PETase-like sequences supplied by project partners
Design and construct expression libraries using molecular cloning, heterologous microbial hosts and high-throughput cell-free expression; establish quality controls for expression, activity and strain or construct validation
Plan and execute rational, directed-evolution and AI-guided enzyme engineering cycles targeting thermostability, catalytic efficiency, substrate engagement and performance on solid PET and capture all strain engineering steps in CellRepo
Develop and validate a tiered screening stack and assays on real post-consumer materials
Implement and troubleshoot automated, miniaturised workflows using platforms such as Opentrons OT-2, acoustic liquid handling and microarray or plate-based robotics, with robust design-of-experiments and batch-effect controls
Capture experimental results as analysis-ready, provenance-rich datasets and close successive DBTL loops by using the data to update candidate ranking and mutation-selection strategies
Evaluate PETase, MHETase/BHETase and PET-directed binding-module combinations, quantify synergy and identify conditions relevant to scalable monomer recovery and circular upcycling routes
Analyse data rigorously, including kinetics, uncertainty, reproducibility and cross-platform or cross-site comparability; maintain excellent laboratory records, code, protocols and standard operating procedures
Work collaboratively across biology, chemistry, engineering, computing and industrial translation; coordinate experiments and exchange of materials and data with EBIC and international partners
Communicate results through peer-reviewed papers, technical reports, conference presentations, stakeholder activities and responsible public engagement, while observing safety, research integrity, data management and Responsible Research and Innovation requirements
Willingness and ability to travel within the UK and internationally, including visits to collaborator laboratories and conferences, as required for the project and subject to reasonable adjustments

 

Additionally, for Senior Research Associate:

 

Provide scientific and technical management for major work packages, defining priorities, decision criteria, risks, resources and delivery plans across the computational, automation and wet-laboratory components
Coordinate partner-facing delivery and translate platform outputs into decision-grade evidence for biofoundry, enzyme-technology, recycling and other industrial stakeholders
Mentor and supervise researchers and students, establish inclusive and reproducible working practices, and build capability across the team
Initiate follow-on research, contribute substantially to grant and associateship applications, and help shape the strategic development and external profile of the EBIC/ICOS programme
Explore and contributes towards technology translation and exploitation

 

 

The Person (Essential)

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

 

Essential for Research Associate and Senior Research Associate:

 

Substantial hands-on research experience in synthetic biology, molecular biology, microbial biotechnology, enzyme engineering, biochemistry or a closely related area
Demonstrable experience of molecular cloning, DNA/RNA manipulation, microbial transformation or genome engineering, cultivation and validation of engineered organisms or constructs
Experience designing and optimising heterologous protein-expression systems and functionally characterising recombinant enzymes
Experience applying directed evolution and/or DBTL workflows, including library design, mutagenesis, high-throughput screening and genotype–phenotype interpretation
Ability to develop robust, reproducible experimental workflows with appropriate controls, traceable records, quantitative analysis and critical troubleshooting
Experience using generative AI for biotechnology and bioinformatics to inform experimental design, such as protein or nucleotide sequence analysis, motif/active-site assessment, clustering, structure prediction or variant prioritisation
Practical computational and data-analysis skills sufficient to create transparent, reusable analyses and to work effectively with computational collaborators; familiarity with Python, R or equivalent tools is advantageous
Evidence of delivering original research to a high standard, normally including peer-reviewed publications and presentation of work at scientific meetings
Ability to manage priorities and milestones independently while contributing constructively to a multidisciplinary, multi-partner research programme
Excellent written and oral communication, including the ability to explain complex experimental and computational work to specialists and non-specialists and to write protocols that other laboratories can reproduce
Ability to undertake laboratory work involving microorganisms, molecular biology and enzyme assays in accordance with institutional risk assessments, training and safety procedures

 

In addition, essential for Senior Research Associate:

 

A sustained record of independent or substantially self-directed research management, with high-quality outputs appropriate to career stage
Experience coordinating complex work packages or collaborative projects, managing scientific risk and coordinating delivery across disciplines or organisations
Experience supervising, mentoring or developing researchers and/or students and promoting an inclusive, high-performing research culture
Evidence of contributing to research funding, partnership development, technology translation, work in or engagement with industrial and other non-academic stakeholders
An additional record of independent research management, supervision and collaborative delivery commensurate with the senior level of the role

 

 

Desirable for both Research Associate and Senior Research Associate:

 

Research experience with PETases, polyester hydrolases, plastic biodegradation, biocatalysis or enzymatic polymer recycling
Experience with microbial strain engineering, cell-free protein expression or rapid prototyping of enzyme variants
Laboratory automation experience, including robotic liquid handling, Opentrons, acoustic dispensing, assay miniaturisation, microarrays or high-throughput plate workflows
Experience developing fluorescence- or absorbance-based enzyme assays and/or chromatographic quantification using HPLC, UPLC, LC or GC

Experience analysing metagenomic data or discovering enzymes from environmental sequence datasets
Experience designing multi-enzyme systems, binding modules, enzyme formulations or process-relevant assays using insoluble substrates
Experience translating synthetic biology or enzyme technologies towards industrial application, including scalability, robustness, downstream-process compatibility or technology-readiness assessment
Experience of international research collaboration, responsible innovation, public engagement or contributing to social-media communication of research
Experience working on relevant industry or commerce setting with goal-oriented and deadline-constrained environment

Independent, resourceful, reliable and able to exercise sound scientific judgement

Able to represent the programme confidently with collaborators, funders, industry and wider stakeholders

postings.advert_text:
Applications are invited for a Research Assistant in the group of Dr Haopeng Yu at the Sainsbury Laboratory Cambridge University (SLCU).

The Yu Group develops AI methods to understand how plants use genetic information to build different cell types, regulate gene expression and respond to their environment. We build interpretable AI and biological foundation models that learn the regulatory "language" of plant genomes and RNA and use them to decode the function of non-coding sequences and to generate hypotheses for experimental testing. The group also develops AI agents as virtual research partners for plant scientists.

More information about the group and Dr Yu's research can be found at: https://www.slcu.cam.ac.uk/research/research-groups/yu-group and https://www.slcu.cam.ac.uk/people/haopeng-yu.

The post holder will contribute to the group's ongoing research projects, including processing and analysing plant genomic and multi-omic data on high-performance computing (HPC) systems, fine-tuning and interpreting AI foundation models, and helping prepare manuscripts and funding applications. This is a fully computational role, suited to candidates with a background or strong interest in bioinformatics and computational biology.

Main responsibilities will include:

Processing and analysing genomic and multi-omic datasets on HPC systems, using bioinformatics tools and pipelines in Bash, Python and/or R
Fine-tuning and interpreting AI foundation models, including preparing and curating training datasets
Working with experimental collaborators to analyse and interpret their data, and to design predictions for experimental testing
Carrying out statistical analysis and keeping clear, reproducible records of code and results
Preparing figures, presenting results to the group, and contributing to manuscripts and funding applications

Candidates should hold a first or Master's degree in bioinformatics, computational biology, plant biology, molecular biology or a related field. Practical experience of bioinformatics analysis and programming in Bash, Python and/or R is essential, together with a foundation in machine learning and an understanding of plant molecular biology and gene regulation. Practical wet-lab experience, which helps in understanding and interpreting experimental data, would be desirable, as would experience with statistical analysis, HPC or deep learning frameworks. Good organisational skills, a high degree of accuracy including outstanding record keeping, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team are essential.

The Laboratory provides a welcoming and collaborative environment with a wide range of family-friendly benefits and development opportunities. More about the Sainsbury Laboratory and details of what the University offers to employees can be found at: http://www.slcu.cam.ac.uk/.

Please ensure that you upload a copy of your full CV, and a cover letter highlighting your suitability for the position and contact information of three referees.

The post is available with a start date as soon as possible.

Fixed-term: The funds for this post are available for 1 year in the first instance.

Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online.

Scientific enquiries apart from the formal application should be directed to Dr Haopeng Yu at hy461@cam.ac.uk (https://www.slcu.cam.ac.uk/people/haopeng-yu).

For questions regarding the application process, please email HR@slcu.cam.ac.uk

Please quote reference PT51536 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy.

The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

 Leeds Beckett University is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Research Fellow to join a multidisciplinary research team undertaking an externally funded systematic review of interventions for fathers and male carers experiencing multiple and complex needs.

 Funded by Foundations, this 12-month project will identify what works, for whom and under what conditions, to inform the development of evidence-based support for fathers, male carers and their families.

 Working across the Carnegie School of Education, School of Health, and School of Social Sciences and Humanities, you will contribute to a systematic review that will inform a subsequent practice review and generate recommendations for professionals working with families experiencing multiple and complex needs. The findings will strengthen the evidence base on parenting support and help inform the development and delivery of interventions that better respond to the needs of fathers, male carers and their families.

 We are looking for a researcher with experience of conducting or contributing to systematic reviews or other evidence synthesis projects, a strong eye for detail and a commitment to producing high-quality research.

 You will have excellent organisational skills and the ability to work accurately and methodically with research evidence. You will be confident working independently and collaboratively, managing competing priorities and contributing effectively to the delivery of a time-limited research project.

 An interest in parenting support, family interventions and the experiences of fathers and male carers with multiple and complex needs would be particularly welcome.

 This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to research with clear potential to inform professional practice and improve support for fathers, male carers and their families.

About the role

Applications are invited for a postdoctoral position in Catherine Jopling’s research group at the University of Nottingham. The position is funded by a BBSRC grant, entitled “Defining the interconnected roles of CCR4-NOT and TENT4/5 proteins in mRNA targeting to the endoplasmic reticulum”, held jointly with Martin Bushell at the CRUK Scotland Institute. The successful applicant will collaborate closely with a second postdoctoral fellow based in the Bushell lab, including reciprocal visits. 

This exciting project will build on recent findings from both labs to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the CCR4-NOT deadenylase complex, the non-canonical poly(A) polymerases TENT4/5 and microRNAs regulate mRNA localisation to, and metabolism at, the endoplasmic reticulum. This is a fundamental molecular biology project that will provide new understanding of essential gene regulation mechanisms but also has potential longer term implications for the development of effective mRNA therapeutics. If successful, you will design and deliver experiments to address these questions using a wide range of techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 genome modification, targeted protein degradation, reporter assays, and RNAseq approaches including SLAMseq and nanopore.

The Jopling lab is part of a thriving Gene Regulation and RNA Biology group in the School of Pharmacy, which was recently awarded Athena Swan Gold status. Our friendly, supportive and inclusive lab is based in the interdisciplinary Biodiscovery Institute on the attractive University Park campus. We are also part of the RNA Interdisciplinary Cluster at Nottingham (RIC@N) network of researchers, providing excellent opportunities for collaboration and interaction.

About you

This position will be an excellent career opportunity for you if you are a highly motivated scientist with a strong interest in mechanisms of RNA regulation. Expertise in molecular biology and cell culture is essential, and experience of CRISPR/Cas9 genome modification, advanced RNA technologies and bioinformatic analysis of RNAseq data would be advantageous. You should also have excellent analytical skills and the ability to communicate well, support others, and work effectively as part of a team.  

What we offer

This fixed-term post is offered for 36 months from 1st November 2026, with some flexibility on the start date. The post is full time (36.25 hours/week); however, we are open to applications for flexible working arrangements and/or part time working. We welcome applications from individuals who do not meet every desirable characteristic but have a strong interest in the project and motivation to learn new skills. We provide generous holiday entitlement of 30 days, plus standard bank holidays and five university closure days including closure between Christmas and New Year.

For more information on the Jopling lab, please see https://joplinglab.com/. 

Informal enquiries may be directed to Catherine.jopling@nottingham.ac.uk. Please note that applications sent directly to this email address will not be accepted.

 Location: John Radcliffe Hospital, Headington, Oxford, OX3 9DU 

 Anti-GD2 immunotherapy has transformed survival rates in children with high-risk neuroblastoma. However, treatment efficacy is limited by high-grade adverse events, in particular neurotoxicity and pain, for reasons that are not fully understood. This project, funded by Medical Research UK, aims to determine the cellular and molecular immune mechanisms underlying neuropathic pain caused by anti-GD2 antibodies. 

 Your primary role will be to establish a behavioural assay of spontaneous pain in a mouse model of neuroblastoma and use this to interrogate the underlying cellular and molecular immune mechanisms evoked by anti-GD2 antibodies. You will work with collaborators to develop and test new antibody derivatives using in vitro and in vivo assays. You will also be responsible for processing and analysing blood samples collected from patients undergoing anti-GD2 therapy for neuroblastoma (Note, this not a patient facing role). 

 You will join a multi-disciplinary team led by UKRI Future Leaders Fellow Dr Alexander Davies, head of the Peripheral Neuroimmunity and Pain Lab at the University of Oxford supported by experts in neurological biomarker detection (Prof Rinaldi), neuroblastoma treatment (Prof Gray), and antibody engineering (Prof Beers). You will attend termly project meetings with the team to share results and receive regular guidance and support. Training will be provided in immune-phenotyping where required. As a postdoctoral researcher you will be encouraged to mentor less experienced members of the research group, as well as gain experience in supervising MSc and summer project students including via the UNIQ+ programme. 

 The Peripheral Neuroimmunity and Pain Lab is part of the Neural Injury Group at NDCN: a highly collaborative group of clinician and non-clinician researchers with complementary expertise in peripheral neuropathy and neuropathic pain. We value teamwork and a community approach to working together in a research laboratory. You will take part in regular presentation and journal club meetings as well as attend yearly networking opportunities such as Oxford Neuroscience, Thomas Willis Day and OxPain events. As a group we subscribe to the University of Oxford Equality and Diversity policy and are committed to providing an environment where everyone feels equal, respected and safe. 

 NDCN has a strong track record of early career researchers transitioning to independence with fair and transparent processes in place to support applications for grants and fellowships as appropriate for each career stage. This project provides the ideal opportunity for a preclinical researcher to gain experience leading a multi-disciplinary project with strong clinical translation. Candidates with a background in either neuroscience or immunology are welcome to apply.

 Please see the below 'Job Description' for further details on the responsibilities and selection criteria, as well as further information about the university and how to apply. 

 For any queries regarding visa sponsorship, HR and the University's Staff Immigration Team will provide advice and assistance when the chosen candidate for the role has been identified. 

 The post is full time for a fixed term until the 30th of June 2028.  

 Only applications received before 12.00 midday on Wednesday 11th of November 2026 will be considered.  

 Interviews will be held as soon as possible thereafter.

Overview

 

Working under the guidance of Professor Mo Zandi and Dr James McGregor, the post-holder will be working on the Great British Chemicals funded project DigiTwin-FT. GBC is a National Research & Innovation Centre for Sustainable Industrial Futures funded by EPSRC and NERC, the centre will unite the UK chemical industry, academic researchers and policy makers to advance innovative, scalable and sustainable technology solutions for defossilising chemicals manufacturing. We aim to create people-focussed opportunities to truly shape sustainable carbon management.

 

The post-holder will be part of the DigiTwin-FT project team working to develop and establish the foundational building block for scaling up CO2-to-fuel Fischer-Tropsch (FT) reactors using a predictive digital twin. Leveraging the University of Sheffield’s existing pilot-scale infrastructure, we will synthesise operational dataset inputs (CO2, H2) to validate a high-fidelity digital twin. Developed in co-creation with our non-academic partner, Siemens, this digital framework will simulate thermo-kinetic behaviours at commercial scales. The project delivers an early-stage techno-economic and life-cycle scoping model, mitigating scale-up risks and accelerating the UK's transition to manufacturing domestic, circular chemicals from waste carbon.

 

The post-holder should have a background in chemical process engineering, with a strong background in process modelling and digital twins. An understanding of carbon dioxide utilisation is preferred though not essential as immersive training will be provided. This is a unique opportunity to work on cutting edge research with some of the leading players in industry and academia with a focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions while creating value added chemicals within a circular carbon economy. The successful candidate will perform digital twin development, data analysis and will be able to gain experience working with Siemens commercial software.

Lead the extraction, cleaning, and structuring of historical and live operational datasets from the pilot-scale Fischer-Tropsch (FT) reactor.

Develop, calibrate, and validate hybrid physics-informed and surrogate models integrating multi-phase fluid dynamics, reaction kinetics, and heat/mass transfer.

Computationally extrapolate the pilot-scale twin to commercial boundary conditions, virtually mapping thermal runaway hotspots, fluid dynamic bottlenecks, and catalyst deactivation profiles.

Execute early-stage TEA and screening LCA scoping models using simulated commercial outputs to evaluate levelised product costs and carbon mitigation metrics.

Drive the day-to-day delivery of Work Packages, taking ownership of deliverables to ensure strict adherence to timelines.

Maintain clean, robust, well-documented, version-controlled code repositories and reproducible data pipelines.

Collaborate directly with industrial partners and software providers (e.g., Siemens) to align digital twin architectures with commercial engineering design workflows.

Coordinate knowledge exchange across the Great British Chemicals (GBC) community, sharing non-proprietary model architectures and methodology frameworks per State Aid guidelines.

Lead the drafting and submission of high-quality research manuscripts for peer-reviewed chemical engineering, process systems, and computational journals.

Work with the PI and University commercialisation officers to identify, document, and protect novel foreground IP (e.g., proprietary kinetic algorithms and reactor control loops).

Assist the team in preparing co-created follow-on research and commercialisation grant proposals leveraging the project's digital baseline.

Embed Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI) and Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (ED&I) principles into activities, making ethical decisions aligned with the University sustainability strategy.

Overview

 

We seek a physicist with expertise in strong light-matter coupling to join a diverse team of researchers working on a dynamic multi-partner research project. The aim of our £7.3 M EPSRC Programme Grant "Molecular Photonic Breadboards" is to develop sustainable photonic materials for use in consumer electronics, solar energy capture and other applications that enable efficient long-range transport of excitation. The successful applicant will hold a PhD qualification, or be close to completion of a relevant PhD, in biotechnology, biochemical engineering, microbiology, industrial biotechnology, chemical engineering or a related discipline.

The ability to plan and carry out laboratory experiments independently, troubleshoot experimental problems and maintain accurate research records is essential.

Expertise in one or more of the following areas will be particularly advantageous: cultivation of magnetotactic bacteria or other microaerophilic microorganisms; controlled bioreactor operation; adaptive laboratory evolution or microbial strain characterisation; cross-flow or tangential-flow filtration; continuous bioprocessing; flow cytometry; microscopy and motility assays; and characterisation of cellular magnetic properties. We are seeking a highly motivated computational researcher for a six-month project in the Marine Behavioural Ecology Group (MBEG), in the Department of Zoology at the University of Cambridge. Undergraduate degrees include BSc Psychology, Psychology with Child Development, Clinical and Community Psychology, and Forensic Psychology. Postgraduate provision encompasses specialised MSc programmes such as Applied Positive Psychology, Business Psychology, and Occupational and Organisational Psychology, alongside conversion courses and MPhil/PhD study. Professionally accredited doctoral programmes in Clinical Psychology and Educational & Child Psychology are regulated by the HCPC and accredited by the BPS.

About the Job

This is a part-time Research Assistant position supporting a 7-month, externally funded research project in Metabolic Psychiatry at the University of East London. The project, “An online psychoeducational and support program implementing ketogenic metabolic therapy for mental illness,” will investigate the implementation and outcomes of an online ketogenic metabolic therapy programme for people experiencing mental illness.

Working closely with the Principal Investigator, Dr Erin Louise Bellamy, the Research Assistant will play a key role in mixed-methods research, including qualitative interviews, thematic analysis, quantitative data analysis, interpretation and reporting of findings, and contributing to academic publications and presentations. The role offers an opportunity for an early-career researcher to gain substantial experience across the full research process within an emerging area of mental health research.

Essential experience required:

A Psychology degree at 2:1 or above.
Experience conducting research interviews, ideally with participants discussing sensitive or personal experiences.
Practical experience conducting thematic analysis of qualitative data.
Experience using SPSS to analyse quantitative data, including appropriate statistical tests such as ANOVAs, and accurately interpreting and reporting results.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to contribute to research reports, academic papers and presentations.
Excellent organisation, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple research tasks and deadlines while working collaboratively with the PI.

About You

The ideal candidate will be an early-career psychology researcher with a strong interest in mental health research and experience across both qualitative and quantitative research methods. You will be confident conducting interviews, analysing qualitative data thematically, and working with quantitative datasets in SPSS. You will have a careful and methodical approach to research, with strong attention to detail and the ability to interpret findings accurately and communicate them clearly.

You will be comfortable working independently while maintaining close collaboration with the Principal Investigator and research participants. As the project involves sensitive mental health topics, you should demonstrate excellent interpersonal skills, professionalism, ethical awareness and an ability to handle confidential information appropriately.

The role would particularly suit someone looking to develop their academic research career and gain experience in mixed-methods research, publication, dissemination and emerging approaches to mental health treatment, in this case, Metabolic Psychiatry. A Master's degree in Psychology would be advantageous.

An interest in, or prior reading around, metabolic psychiatry and ketogenic metabolic therapies for mental health would be desirable but is not essential. What matters most is a strong research foundation, intellectual curiosity, and enthusiasm for contributing to a developing area of mental health science.

About the role

Cholesterol has long been dismissed as little more than membrane scaffolding. This Wellcome Trust-funded Postdoctoral Research Associate post sets out to prove otherwise — revealing how cholesterol acts as an allosteric modulator of GLP-1 receptor (GLP1R) signalling, and tracing what that means for one of the lung's most exposed tissues: the alveolar epithelium. Working within a world-leading, highly collaborative research group at Imperial College London, you will combine advanced single-molecule and fluorescence fluctuation microscopy with the development of a bespoke Alveolus-on-a-Chip — a breathing, physiologically faithful model built to host receptor biology in a setting far closer to its native context than a dish ever could. Over this 24-month post, your findings will open a genuinely new route into understanding — and one day therapeutically targeting — GLP1R signalling in the lung.

What you would be doing

In this role, you will lead investigations into how membrane cholesterol allosterically shapes GLP1R conformational dynamics and downstream signalling, using advanced microscopy, fluorescence fluctuation spectroscopy (FCS/FCCS, RICS, N&B) and spectral-lifetime imaging (FLIM/phasor analysis).

You will design, fabricate and validate an Alveolus-on-a-Chip platform capable of sustaining physiologically representative alveolar epithelial cells under breathing-mimetic conditions, and integrate your molecular pharmacology findings with this organ-on-chip system to determine how cholesterol-dependent GLP1R signalling shapes epithelial responses at the tissue level.

Throughout, you will develop advanced analytical and bioengineering expertise, working in close collaboration with international partners across structural pharmacology, computational membrane biophysics and photonics.

What we are looking for

We are looking for an ambitious and highly motivated postdoctoral researcher with a PhD in pharmacology, biophysics, cell biology, or bioengineering to join this collaborative project. While a full person specification is available in the job description, we are specifically looking for candidates who can demonstrate:

Proven experience in membrane biophysics, receptor pharmacology, or GPCR signalling research.
Technical proficiency in advanced fluorescence microscopy techniques, such as FCS/FCCS, FLIM, super-resolution/STED, or phasor analysis.
Experience with epithelial cell culture and standard molecular and cell biology techniques.
An appetite for organ-on-chip or microfluidic platform design, fabrication, or operation — prior hands-on experience is a plus but not essential.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to interpret quantitative imaging and biophysical datasets.
A collaborative and proactive mindset, with the ability to work across disciplinary boundaries and a commitment to preparing high-quality manuscripts for publication.
The ambition to develop an independent research niche, demonstrating the drive to prepare for a future independent academic career.

What we can offer you

By joining this project, you will benefit from a wealth of professional and scientific opportunities designed to launch your career as an independent investigator:

A high-impact, multidisciplinary environment, working directly with Dr Jorge Bernardino de la Serna (Imperial College London) and collaborating with Prof. Alejandra Tomas (Department of Metabolism, Digestion and Reproduction, Imperial) on the molecular pharmacology of GLP1R and related signalling.
Access to cutting-edge technology, including advanced fluorescence fluctuation and spectral-lifetime microscopy platforms, and the opportunity to help build a bespoke Alveolus-on-a-Chip system from the ground up.
Translational research impact, contributing to a project with real relevance for lung-directed therapeutics and metabolic-respiratory biology.
Scientific recognition and dissemination. You will be responsible for reporting your findings in high-quality manuscripts and presenting your work at national and international conferences.
A collaborative, international network spanning advanced microscopy, membrane biophysics and computational modelling across Europe and beyond.
Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 39 days off a year).
Structured career development. This 24-month post is designed to help you develop independent research ideas and a distinctive scientific niche, preparing you for future academic positions.

About us

The Cancer Antibody Discovery & Immunotherapy group headed by Professor Sophia Karagiannis at St John’s Institute of Dermatology, School of Basic and Medical Biosciences, specialises in dissecting B cell and antibody immune responses and designing therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, derivatives and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), focusing on skin, ovarian and breast cancers. Our research also aims to understand how cancer cells interfere with anti-tumoral immune effector cell functions and apply this knowledge to inform the design of novel antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates with improved efficacy against tumours. The Karagiannis team is the first to design, evaluate and translate anti-tumour IgE class antibodies from concept to clinical testing and commercialization.

About the role

The antibody discovery group at St. John’s Institute of Dermatology and the Breast Cancer Now Unit at King’s College London wishes to appoint a Postdoctoral Research Associate with knowledge of cancer immunology, and experience in antibody immunology and immunotherapy, antibody-drug conjugate generation and antibody functional evaluations, to join its Cancer Antibody Discovery & Immunotherapy research programme. The work will be integrated into the team’s on-going translational activities that include: a) Dissecting the cross-talk between human immunity and breast cancer and utilising this knowledge to develop and evaluate more effective antibodies as diagnostics or therapeutics, b) Engineering and studying antibodies with modified Fc regions to better engage immune effector cells against cancer, and antibody-drug conjugates for cancer therapy, c) Translation of novel antibody candidates to first-in-man clinical studies with clinical and academic colleagues at Guy’s Hospital.

The postholder will have a strong background in antibody immunology/biology and functional evaluations of antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates. They will conduct cutting edge research into cancer immunotherapy using novel Fc engineered antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates that recognise cell surface tumour antigens overexpressed in breast cancers. This will involve efficacy and mechanism of action evaluations of novel agents conducting several functional assays using patient and healthy volunteer blood and in disease-relevant ex vivo organoid models to support future evaluations in pre-clinical development and clinical study stages of lead molecules. There will be extensive study of human immune cells such as NK cells, monocytes and macrophages, flow cytometric analyses, ELISA style and functional cell-based assays.

The postholder will be fully integrated into the academic team’s antibody immunotherapy translational research programme led by Prof. Sophia Karagiannis at the Guy’s Hospital Campus, forming part of the Beast Cancer Now funded programme at King’s College London. Are you an ambitious researcher looking for your next challenge? Do you have an established background in cryoEM and want to help to develop new routes to combat amyloid diseases? Do you want to further your career in one of the UKs leading research intensive Universities?

We are looking for an outstanding research fellow to join our interdisciplinary team that is investigating how proteins aggregate into amyloid fibrils, and how fibrils with different structure perturb cellular function. Research Fellow in Immunosuppressant Therapeutic Drug Monitoring
Do you have an interest in diagnostics applications? Would you like to be involved in a multidisciplinary project to develop an immunosuppressant therapeutic drug monitoring sensor to provide better patient care?

We are a multidisciplinary team of researchers focusing on the development of in vitro diagnostics assays and devices to deliver better therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) – this can optimise antibiotic use which will help combat AMR, or ensure accurate dosing can be achieved where therapeutic windows are narrow such as in immunosuppressants – this will significantly improve health outcomes. The Role

 

We are excited to offer an opportunity for a Research Assistant/ Associate in Neuromuscular Diseases to join the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre (JWMDRC) at Newcastle University.

 

The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary and internationally recognised research environment bringing together clinicians, basic scientists, bioinformaticians, computational biologists and clinical trial specialists, all working towards the development of innovative therapies for rare neuromuscular diseases.

 

This 18-month full time fixed position is funded through two industry-supported translational research projects focused on the development of novel therapies to reduce fibrosis and fatty replacement in muscular dystrophies.

 

The successful applicant will contribute to the preclinical development of innovative therapeutic approaches for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and limb girdle muscular dystrophies (LGMDs). The work will involve the isolation and characterisation of primary human muscle cells, including fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), establishment of cellular disease models, assessment of drug efficacy and cytotoxicity, immunofluorescence and molecular assays, and evaluation of therapeutic candidates in murine models.

 

The postholder will have the opportunity to participate in every stage of the translational research pipeline, from experiments using patient-derived samples through to in vivo preclinical studies. The projects are delivered in close collaboration with pharmaceutical partners, providing valuable exposure to industry-led drug development and opportunities to interact with external collaborators.

 

What we offer

 

The successful candidate will benefit from working within one of Europe's leading neuromuscular research centres, with access to state-of-the-art facilities, unique patient-derived resources, and an extensive international collaborative network. This role offers an excellent opportunity to gain experience in translational drug development for rare diseases while contributing to projects with clear clinical impact.

 

As this is a laboratory-based role involving human tissue, advanced cell biology techniques and preclinical animal studies, with defined project milestones and ambitious timelines, the successful candidate will be expected to work on-site at the John Walton Muscular Dystrophy Research Centre. The post is therefore not suitable for part-time or remote working.

Your experience in cell biology, including mammalian cell culture and relevant laboratory techniques.
Your experience working with primary human tissues or primary cell isolation, where applicable.
Your experience in planning and delivering independent research projects, including examples of meeting project milestones or deadlines.
Your motivation for applying for this position and your interest in translational research in neuromuscular diseases.

Overview

 

We are recruiting for a dedicated Research Associate on a EPSRC project which aims to improve seismic safety and resilience of communities living in Uganda. This project provides a unique opportunity and platform to contribute to research and development of seismic hazard, vulnerability and exposure models to understand risk in Uganda and enhance the resilience of the country against earthquakes.

 

You will take an active role in analysing, categorising and documenting the collected data, developing of vulnerability/fragility curves using numerical methods, implementing exposure models, performing risk calculations and developing seismic risk management strategies by closely working with academic research teams in Uganda.

 Applications are invited from researchers to work as a Post-Doctoral Research Fellow in the University of Southampton’s world-leading Geochemistry Research Group ( https://www.southampton.ac.uk/oes/research/groups/geochemistry.page ) in the School of Ocean and Earth Science at the National Oceanography Centre Southampton. You will join a community of >500 researchers and support staff drawn from physics, chemistry, biology, geoscience, and engineering, with a strong focus on marine biology and marine environments, to work in a project at the interface between geochemistry, palaeoclimate, and biomineralisation.

 This post is funded through an ERC-selected Starting Grant to Dr David Evans ( https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/62c7dp/doctor-david-evans ) but additionally involves a number of researchers from within the School and is closely linked to a growing team at the University of Southampton focused on driving forward the societal impact of palaeoclimate datasets by mechanistically understanding biomineralisation processes and boundary condition changes, funded via both the Royal Society and Dr Evans’ ERC-selected Starting Grant.

 Our group’s research focuses in part on the use of biomineral geochemistry to infer ion transport processes during calcification, because the (trace) metal composition of the shell or skeleton must be controlled by the composition of the fluid at the site of calcification and the way in which ions are transported in and out of this enclosed space. However, it is increasingly recognised that most biominerals are formed via an amorphous or metastable precursor phase, which may impart an additional fractionation and complicate the interpretation of biomineral metal chemistry, yet the geochemical details of this process are poorly understood.

 In this project, the applicant will address this knowledge gap via the experimental formation and characterisation of amorphous and crystalline materials under a wide range of conditions, including in situ techniques in collaboration with colleagues in the Institute of Life Sciences and utilising the School’s state of the art cryo-electron microscopy facility. Ultimately, the goal is to determine whether inorganic processes alone might be sufficient to explain the shell chemistry of calcifying marine organisms, and to build these findings into a geochemical biomineralisation model.

 A successful candidate should have:

 A PhD (or equivalent) in geochemistry.

 Experience in the operation of single and/or multi-collector plasma mass spectrometer instruments, ideally including associated clean laboratory sample preparation.

 Experience in applying geochemical tools to constraining past environmental, oceanographic, or climatic change.

 Experience in geochemical box modelling, or an enthusiasm for developing these skills.

 Skills in hypothesis-testing, experiment design, analysis of data sets and writing scientific manuscripts and reports.

 And should additionally:

 Demonstrate strong drive, ambition and motivation, with the capacity to deliver on challenging tasks and to meet deadlines both individually and as working as part of a team.

 Express a desire to apply cutting edge geochemical techniques to understanding marine biomineralisation.

 This post is a fixed-term appointment for two years.

 For further enquiries please contact Dr David Evans ( d.evans@soton.ac.uk )

ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY

Swansea University is a research-led university that has been making a difference since 1920. The University community thrives on exploration and discovery and offers the right balance of excellent teaching and research, matched by an enviable quality of life.

Our stunning waterfront campuses and multicultural community make us a desirable workplace for colleagues from around the world. Our reward and benefits, and ways of working enable those who join us to have enriching careers, matched by an excellent work-life balance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a dynamic and committed Teaching Fellow in Psychology to contribute to our undergraduate and postgraduate teaching portfolio, including areas such as research methods, health and wellbeing, and environmental psychology. This fixed-term post is to provide teaching cover during a funded academic secondment and is available for up to 0.4 FTE from 4 January 2027 to 31 August 2027.

The successful candidate will join a vibrant and supportive academic community within the School of Psychology, part of the Faculty of Medicine, Health and Life Science. The postholder will contribute to teaching and learning in various settings, including (but not limited to) small tutorial groups, seminars, workshops, and practical classes. Responsibilities may also include marking student work, developing and updating teaching materials, designing and marking assessments, providing timely and constructive feedback, responding to student enquiries, and participating in meetings with staff and students as required. In addition, the Teaching Fellow may be involved in recruitment, outreach, and other student-facing support activities.

This role would suit a current PhD candidate or recent graduate with teaching experience. While the post is available at 0.4 FTE, we are open to appointing more than one candidate on a fractional basis, up to the combined FTE. Swansea University is dedicated to providing an excellent student experience. We are looking for individuals with a passion for education who are committed to innovative, student-centred teaching.

We aim to establish an inclusive environment and welcome diverse applications from the following protected characteristics: age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race (including colour, nationality, ethnic and national origin), religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.

As an inclusive and welcoming workplace, we value people for their skills regardless of their background. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English.

WELSH LANGUAGE SKILLS

The Welsh language level required for this role is Level 1 - A little. The role holder will be able to pronounce Welsh words, answer the phone in Welsh (good morning/afternoon) and use very basic everyday words and phrases (thank you, please etc.). Level 1 can be reached by completing a 1 hour course.

The University is a proud bilingual institution, our Welsh Language Strategy outlines our aspiration to promote the language and enable our staff to engage with the language as an additional workplace skill and as a gateway to new cultural and social opportunities. Applications are welcome in Welsh and will not be treated less favourably than those submitted in English. Welsh speakers have the right to an interview in Welsh. Applicants for a role where Welsh skills are essential are expected to present their application in Welsh and will be interviewed in Welsh, if shortlisted.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Applications for this role will take the format of a CV submission and cover letter.

Applicants are encouraged to attach a covering letter outlining their teaching experience and availability, along with a CV. Please also indicate whether you are applying for the full 0.4 FTE post or a smaller fractional appointment.

 About us 

 UCL School of Pharmacy is one of the world’s leading centres of excellence for pharmaceutical science, education and professional engagement, ranked third in the world by QS (2025, Pharmacy and Pharmacology). The Division has a track record in high-quality research across a broad range of drug discovery, pharmacy and patient safety-related areas, and for developing spinout companies that have brought new therapeutic strategies to patients.

 Further information can be found on our website http://www.ucl.ac.uk/pharmacy/ 
 This is an exciting opportunity to join the Dziemidowicz group at UCL School of Pharmacy. You will work on a Little Princess Trust-funded project developing an injectable "smart" hydrogel to co-deliver CAR-T cells and checkpoint inhibitors for the treatment of childhood diffuse midline glioma, as part of a collaborative team involving UCL Pharmaceutics and Great Ormond Street Hospital.

 About the role 

 This is a 7 month fixed-term role due to available funding, in the first instance.

 You will carry out the laboratory work behind a translational drug delivery project, formulating and characterising a polymer-nanoparticle hydrogel designed for convection-enhanced delivery, and testing its ability to preserve CAR-T cell viability and function alongside sustained checkpoint inhibitor release.

 Day-to-day work will include: hydrogel synthesis and rheological characterisation, cell culture (T cells, DMG cell lines), assays such as ELISA, flow cytometry and cytotoxicity/viability testing.

 You'll work closely with Dr Karolina Dziemidowicz and Dr Chris Morris, with input from clinical collaborators at GOSH, in a supportive, multidisciplinary environment spanning biomaterials, immunology and translational neuro-oncology. This is a hands-on laboratory role suited to someone who is keen to contribute directly to early-stage cancer therapeutics research with a clear path towards in vivo studies and clinical translation.

 About you 

 We are looking for a candidate with PhD-level experience in pharmacy, pharmaceutical science, chemistry, biomedical engineering, or a related discipline. If you do not hold a PhD, you will be appointed as a Research Assistant on Grade 6B and regraded to Research Fellow - Grade 7, upon successful completion of your PhD.

 Excellent interpersonal and strong communication skills will be highly regarded, as the project involves engagement with patients and families – empathy, comfort and sensitivity in these settings is essential. Confident working independently once trained, while contributing openly to a small, close-knit team. The candidate will be expected to deliver robust, reproducible proof-of-concept data across the project's work packages to time

 The candidate should also be trained in aseptic cell culture technique and familiarity with standard immunoassays (ELISA, flow cytometry). It is desirable that the successful postholder will have experience with hydrogel/biomaterial formulation, antibody drug delivery, CAR-T or T-cell work, or convection-enhanced delivery systems, but training will be provided if not.

 The post-holder is expected to analyse and present data on a regular basis. This will include presentations at lab, departmental, project and funder meetings. In addition, the post-holder is expected to draft scientific reports for the funder and manuscripts for publication. The interaction in a collaborative fashion with other members of the lab and wider collaborative network is also expected.

Hours: Full-time, 36.5 hours per week (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Thursday 19 November 2026, 11:59 PM (UK)                        

Full time Salary Range: £31,861.00 - £35,302.00 per annum

About the Role

A senior technician is required to provide support for the European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant RHYTHMS, ‘Rhizosphere Rhythms: Unravelling Diurnal Microbiome Dynamics and Their Role in Plant-Soil Interactions’, within Professor Gary Bending’s research group in the School of Life Sciences. The research explores how plant circadian rhythms influence rhizosphere microbial communities, nitrogen cycling and interactions with bacteriophages.

 

You will work closely with postdoctoral researchers, students and collaborators to set-up and maintain plant-microbe experiments in controlled environments and the field, undertake microbiological, molecular and environmental analyses, coordinate sampling programmes, and lead the organisation and management of experimental samples and associated data.

 

You will help establish and maintain plant and soil microcosms, synthetic microbial communities and controlled-environment experiments, as well as support field trials. You will also help organise carefully timed sampling campaigns. Your laboratory work will include microbial culture, sample processing and quantification, extraction and quality assessment of DNA and RNA, PCR/qPCR and preparation of material for downstream sequencing and chemical / metabolite analyses. You may also contribute to measurements of root-zone physico-chemical conditions and nitrogen cycling, and to the organisation and preliminary analysis of microbiome and environmental datasets. You will take a lead role in maintaining and organising samples, experimental metadata and research records

 

You will join the Bending group/team in the School of Life Sciences at Warwick University.

 

Any requests for further information about the role can be directed to Prof. Gary Bending (gary.bending@warwick.ac.uk)

 

We and the wider University of Warwick environment offer substantial opportunities for professional development including regular opportunities to attend international conferences.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

We are seeking to appoint a senior research technician to join Professor Gary Bending’s RHYTHMS research team in the School of Life Sciences at the University of Warwick. Funded by a European Research Council Advanced Grant, the project will investigate how daily rhythms in plants influence the composition and activity of microbes around their roots, and the implications for nutrient cycling and sustainable agriculture.

 

The successful candidate should have a relevant degree or equivalent knowledge and practical experience, expertise working with microorganisms and a methodical approach to planning experiments and recording results.

 

You should be comfortable working both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Experience of plant growth experiments, environmental sampling, molecular biology, research data management and preparation of health and safety documentation will be advantageous. Training and opportunities to develop new skills will be available.

 

This is an opportunity to contribute to ambitious, internationally relevant research at the interface of plant biology, microbial ecology and soil science, while developing a broad range of specialist technical and research-management skills.

About the Department

The School of Life Sciences (SLS) is a cohesive, enthusiastic community producing world-class, high-impact bioscience research and teaching within an open, friendly, inclusive and highly collaborative environment.

For further information about the School of Life Sciences please see our website at:

http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/lifesci

 

We believe that collegiality, openness, inclusivity and diversity are essential for an excellent research and teaching environment. Our workplace ethic has enabled us to gain the Athena SWAN Silver award. We are dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage applications from all groups with protected characteristics traditionally under-represented in STEM fields. As part of our ongoing commitment to addressing gender equality under the Athena Swan chartermark, we would particularly encourage and welcome applications from female academics. In your application, you can also include any career breaks you may have taken (e.g. parental/caring/long-term sick leave, part-time work, secondments) or any periods where you were unable or restricted to work because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter on the closing date stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications

 

Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.

 

Your cover letter should detail your motivation for applying for the role as well as detailing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria.   

 

The interviews will be held: To Be Confirmed

 

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. About the Role

3 Year Fixed Term Position

 

This is an exciting opportunity to be involved with a pan-European project working on the containment and control of key plant pathogens/pests. The role requires the ability to generate detailed mechanistic models, to develop highly efficient code to simulate spatio-temporal spread and control, to fit such models to data and to consider robust and effective control strategies.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work with world-leading leading mathematical modellers, plant scientists and practical pest managers from across Europe and to help influence policy.

There is considerable scope to develop and extend a range of models in a number of novel directions.

 

Informal enquiries to be sent to Professor Matt Keeling - m.j.keeling@warwick.ac.uk

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

Candidates need to have a strong quantitative and computational background and ideally experience with epidemiological modelling. The successful candidate will need to be able to develop novel models (or extend existing models) to capture the know biology of different invasive pests, and to develop highly efficient code that can be incorporated into user-friendly platforms. Strong communication skills are also important, as the successful candidate will need to interact with academics and stakeholders from a variety of disciplines.

 

Experience with handling complex data and fitting mathematical models to data would be an advantage. An interest in plant pests and diseases, or a willingness to learn, would also be helpful. An ideal candidate would also have experience of working in a team environment, as well as being able to develop their own ideas.

Warwick Medical School has an excellent reputation for our distinctive portfolio of high-quality education programmes and for the excellence and global impact of our research.

Warwick Clinical Trials Unit (WCTU) has a proven track record in delivering high-quality research.  Our specialties include Cancer, Emergency and Critical Care, Surgery Pain and Rehabilitation and Methodology.

 

Our vision is to lead world class clinical trials which transform the lives of patients. We are a strong, vibrant and enthusiastic team; we are proud of our interdisciplinary, inclusive, and collaborative approach and have established a thriving community of over 160 staff consisting of clinical trialists, statisticians, economists, clinicians, and operational teams.

 

Warwick CTU operates across two campuses: the Gibbet Hill Campus, University of Warwick and University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire.

 

 WMS offers academic education across several levels and is the UK leader for graduate entry medicine.  Our portfolio of postgraduate programmes aims to provide excellent education and continued professional development for healthcare professionals across a number of areas, including advanced clinical and critical care practice, diabetes, leadership, medical education, interdisciplinary biomedical research, public health and health research.  We have expanded our education portfolio to include two innovative undergraduate courses: MSci Integrated Natural Sciences and BSc Health and Medical Sciences.  We also offer full and part time research degrees either at Warwick Medical School or in a clinical setting, encompassing PhDs, MD Doctor of Medicine, PhD by Published Work, and MSc by Research.

This post offers an exceptional opportunity to contribute to housing research, expand your research profile, and play a key role in the growth of a dynamic research lab within a world-leading art and design institution.
